Hi.

On Thu, Jan 28, 2010 at 4:58 PM, branko <b.mi...@lumc.nl> wrote:
> Hi all,

[snip]

> 3) Few  questions regarding Quality checks and basic data
> manipulations in Aroma:
>    I would like to give meaningful labels to  the Arrays in the e.g.
> box-plots (instead of CEL file names, as said i have 300) .
>    How can I do that?
>    Also how can I sort them ?

Please show code what you are using/trying to do. I will assume that
you are trying to use, say, plotRle(), as illustrated in Vignette
'Human exon array analysis' [http://aroma-project.org/node/37]. The
names and the ordering of the arrays/samples is given by the
input/source data set. For instance, if you do:

qa <- QualityAssessmentModel(plm);
plotRle(qa);

then the names and the ordering is given by the chip-effect set of the
ProbeLevelModel 'plm':

ces <- getChipEffectSet(plm);
print(getNames(ces));

The easiest way to reorder or plot a subset of the arrays in the boxplot, use:

plotRle(qa, arrays=c(3:5, 2, 4,1));

Renaming the arrays is slightly trickier - the best it to make sure
have the correct names in the chip effect set 'ces'. You can override
the defaults names using full names translators, cf. how to 'Use
fullname translators to rename data files':
http://aroma-project.org/node/85. It's a fairly advanced feature,
and I let you play with it to figure it out, but you can rename
everything whatever you want if you know what you do and are careful.

Probably an easier solution is to avoid adding the labels when
plotting, and then add them "manually";

Example:

# First an ad hoc workaround (next release will have this built-in)
boxplot.stats <- appendVarArgs(boxplot.stats);

names <- getNames(ces); # or whatever names you want to use
arrays <- c(5,2:4);
plotRle(qa, arrays=arrays, show.names=FALSE);
axis(side=1, at=seq(along=arrays), labels=names[arrays], las=2);

/Henrik
